title: ALISA: Accelerating Large Language Model Inference via Sparsity-Aware KV Caching
problem: KV caching for LLM inference requires growing memory as sequences lengthen, causing I/O bottlenecks and out-of-memory errors on resource-constrained systems despite its linear-complexity memory access benefits. The memory overhead becomes a throughput bottleneck, limiting practical deployment on single commodity GPUs.
motivation: LLMs are accurate and widely deployed but memory-intensive for autoregressive inference, making efficient KV cache management critical for deployment on resource-constrained systems.
method: ALISA combines algorithm-level optimization with system-level scheduling. The Sparse Window Attention (SWA) algorithm prioritizes important tokens and reduces KV cache memory footprint with negligible accuracy loss. The system employs three-phase token-level dynamic scheduling to optimize the trade-off between caching and recomputation, maximizing throughput on resource-constrained GPU-CPU systems.
key_novelty: Algorithm-system co-design combining sparse attention patterns with dynamic token-level scheduling to optimize KV cache memory usage and throughput on resource-constrained inference.
contributions: Sparse Window Attention (SWA) algorithm that reduces KV cache memory with minimal accuracy loss
Three-phase token-level dynamic scheduling strategy optimizing cache versus recomputation trade-offs
3x throughput improvement over FlexGen and 1.9x over vLLM on single GPU-CPU systems
primary_theme: KV cache optimization via attention sparsity and dynamic scheduling
